question: Can a complete recorded acoustic+visual pair be extracted at every authentic site×date, and how much full four-method source-positive evidence would be lost or retained in such a strictly paired recorded-method panel?

source.authors: Wenner et al. (2025), Global Ecology and Conservation 62 e03837
source.original_methods_statement: Paper §2.2 says acoustic, visual and dipnet used in each ordinary field survey; missing dipnet method rows in released CSV do not prove dipnet was not deployed.

fixed_inputs.source_positive: native count>0 on at least one original raw row for site×species or site×date×species; Boolean OR
fixed_inputs.uniqueness: require exactly one acoustic and one visual CSV row for every site×date; fail closed for duplicates or missing pairs

endpoints_fixed: Count site×date groups with exactly one row of each core method (full coverage contract).
Compare original all-method source-positive site×species sets with acoustic+visual-only sets, at cohort and species level, including losses exclusive to aquatic methods.
Compare original all-method source-positive site×date×species sets with paired-core positives, reporting method-specific daily complementary detection.
Record source-count per method and exact raw-row ID and date in an auditable 2-method×date×species long CSV.
Track original method rows for dipnet and bottletrap separately; missing row means NOT REPRESENTED IN CSV, not evidence method was not actually deployed in the field.
Conserve no source evidence by modification: everything is an analysis view, not a changed original dataset.
stop: This is post-exposure: exploratory values have been inspected and CI assertions validate replay, not preregistered external hypothesis support.
Recorded core method rows across all dates do not certify comparable effort, observer duration, method deployment or detection independence.
Original article reports dipnet use on all standard visits despite many CSV dates having no dipnet row: cannot call missing row a method not conducted.
AV source-positive subset omissions are unknown/not detected by paired methods, not true biological absence.
Species-dependent detectability can cause group-level shifts; do not claim causal habitat filter, movement M, biotic interactions, or restoration treatment effect.
No original unmarked coefficient estimation or new fourth EOG-WF scored endpoint. Leave PR Draft/unmerged.
